title: Reduce Manual Work Across the Everpure Platform
summary: Discover how August 2026 updates to the Everpure Platform reduce manual effort with improved storage efficiency, smarter automation, simpler migrations, and stronger data protection.
body_markdown:
### Summary


Everpure platform updates in August 2026 include improved storage efficiency, AI-driven fleet automation, faster VMware-to-OpenShift migrations, stronger Kubernetes data protection, and simpler Azure VM storage management.


### August 2026 Recap


August’s launch is about making your day-to-day work easier. Whether that means greater capacity density helping you store more of your data on one array, automating aspects of fleet management, or an easier way to manage VMs, we’re reducing the amount of work *you* need to do and multiplying your results.


Let’s get into exactly how.


## **More capacity and throughput from the same hardware**


### Get more from data that is already reduced


Backup, archive, and AI corpus data usually arrives already compressed or already reduced by the application that wrote it. Exact-match deduplication finds almost nothing left to remove.[Purity DeepReduce](https://blog.everpuredata.com/perspectives/next-frontier-in-data-efficiency/) ™ now extends to new FlashBlade//S200R1 and FlashBlade//S500R2 deployments, matching each chunk against the closest similar content anywhere in the cluster and storing only the byte-level difference. Estimator runs on production systems show a median 2:1 reduction beyond the compression already present, helping teams hold more data on the same raw flash.


### Push more throughput through a single namespace


Consolidating onto one large namespace is simpler to operate than sharding a workload across many filesystems. It only works if that namespace can absorb the throughput. FlashBlade//S500R2 now adds four CPU cores per node, raising overall single-namespace throughput by roughly 15%. Write-intensive workloads benefit most, letting teams consolidate analytics and AI data sets without redesigning how the data is laid out.


[Upgrade your Purity environment today](http://pure1.purestorage.com/) ! (Pure1® login required)


## **One control plane for a larger fleet**


### Manage twice the arrays as a single pool


At a certain scale, storage management stops being a technical problem and becomes an organizational one. Every array added to the estate is another boundary to manage, and another point of friction when workloads need to move.[Everpure Fusion](https://www.everpuredata.com/products/automation-orchestration.html) ™ now doubles the number of arrays under a single management plane that operates as one pool of storage. Placement is AI-driven, based on real-time array health and capacity. Policies are defined once and propagate across every array.


### Match workloads to the right fault domain


Placement decisions affect residency, isolation, latency, and consistency. That context usually lives in tribal knowledge and scripts rather than in provisioning. New topology groups give Everpure Fusion the context to guide workloads onto infrastructure that meets geographic, physical, or logical criteria, improving VMware datastore placement, strengthening data residency controls, and enhancing data locality for applications. Fleet structure becomes a managed object with a shared source of truth that exports to CMDB, which cuts script sprawl.


## **Continuous access for file workloads**


### Keep file access through a site outage


Failing over file services has usually meant remounting shares and repointing paths, which turns a storage event into an application outage. ActiveCluster™ solves this for block workloads. Two arrays stay synchronously replicated, and both sides serve the same data at the same time. Losing one means no manual failover and no data in flight to lose.


[ActiveCluster for file](https://blog.everpuredata.com/purely-technical/continuity-with-active-cluster/) extends that architecture to file, delivering synchronous replication and continuous access across sites as a native Purity data service. Applications and users keep access through maintenance events, infrastructure failures, and site outages. No remounting, no new file paths.


### Make availability a policy, not a runbook


Availability has traditionally been assembled site by site: failover runbooks, replication topologies, configurations that differ by location. ActiveCluster for file makes it a fleet-wide policy instead, managed through Everpure Fusion, with automatic failover and transparent mobility. Critical file workloads are protected with zero RPO. Teams get consistent application behavior across locations without maintaining the scaffolding that used to deliver it. Customers can activate the capability themselves.


## **A simpler path from VMware to OpenShift**


As organizations modernize their virtualization strategy, more teams are moving VMware workloads to[Red Hat OpenShift Virtualization](https://www.redhat.com/en/technologies/cloud-computing/openshift/virtualization) . The destination is compelling. The migration itself shouldn’t be the obstacle. We’re working closely with Red Hat to integrate[FlashArray](https://www.everpuredata.com/products/block-file-object-storage.html) ™ with the Migration Toolkit for Virtualization (MTV), so workloads move onto OpenShift efficiently, quickly, and safely. This release focuses on cold migration, and the integrations are in place to support it.


### Migrate VMs in minutes, not hours


Traditional migrations copy VM disk data over the network, and at enterprise scale, that means long windows and congested infrastructure. With storage copy offload, MTV hands the data movement to FlashArray, which uses its native XCOPY support to copy the source virtual disk’s data straight onto the OpenShift persistent volume, volume-to-volume, entirely inside the array. The bulk disk data never traverses the production network, so migrations that once took hours can complete in minutes, and the network stays free for production traffic.


### Land workloads in the correct FlashArray pod


Fast migration shouldn’t force placement compromises. New cross-pod XCOPY support extends offload acceleration to migrations where the source and target volumes live in different FlashArray pods, so teams can organize migrated workloads into the pods that match their needs from day one, without giving up the speed advantage.


### Automation that reduces risk


Speed matters, but so does getting every VM across intact. Because the migration runs through MTV migration plans backed by array-level data movement, completeness is easy to maintain and manual steps are kept to a minimum. Fewer hands-on interventions mean fewer opportunities for error, making a large-scale migration something you can schedule with confidence rather than brace for.


## **Stronger protection for Kubernetes data**


### Capture every volume at the same instant


Standard CSI snapshots operate at the individual persistent volume level. That works for single-volume applications and falls short for databases, virtual machines, and SAP or Oracle deployments that span several volumes. Snapshot each volume independently, even milliseconds apart, and the recovery point can be inconsistent. PX-CSI 26.2.0 implements the Kubernetes VolumeGroupSnapshot API for FlashArray block volumes. Kubernetes submits a single request, and PX-CSI uses the array’s native consistency group capability to capture every volume at the same point in time. It does not quiesce the application, so this is crash-consistent rather than application-consistent. That is still a reliable foundation for backup, disaster recovery, cloning, and restore.


### Manage tenant backups without holding their secrets


A managed service provider operates the Kubernetes platform but does not own what runs on it. Holding customer backup targets or credentials creates liability.[Portworx Backup](https://portworx.com/products/portworx-backup/) adds federated mode, a secretless architecture that isolates credentials and backup locations from the provider’s view. Federated mode currently covers Gardener and Garden Linux workloads on Azure, GCP, and AWS. Providers keep fleet-wide policy, scheduling, and visibility, and customers retain custody of sensitive information.


[Learn more about Portworx Backup for service providers](https://portworx.com/blog/portworx-backup-3-0-0-service-providers/)


## **More control and lower cost in the cloud**


### Keep Lambda functions inside your own VPC


For security-conscious enterprises, where a cloud component executes is not a small detail. It decides whether the deployment passes review. When policy requires AWS Lambda functions to run inside a designated VPC, anything outside that boundary becomes an adoption barrier. Everpure Cloud Dedicated for AWS now deploys all associated Lambda functions within your VPC by default. The capability ships in Purity//FA 6.12.birch, supporting enterprise security, compliance, and network isolation requirements.


### Cut Azure VM storage costs as workloads grow


As cloud workloads grow, teams need storage that scales alongside their applications without adding cost or operational complexity. Now generally available, Everpure Cloud Azure Native for Azure VMs is a fully managed enterprise block storage service jointly engineered by Everpure and Microsoft. Volumes attach to Windows or Linux VMs through native Azure workflows. Thin provisioning and data reduction help optimize utilization and reduce storage costs by up to 40%, while capacity and performance scale to meet workload requirements. The service is available through Azure Marketplace, integrates with Azure networking, and is live in[supported Azure regions](https://support.everpuredata.com/r/everpure-cloud-azure-native/azure-regions-support) .


### Connect Azure VMs without host-side scripts


Host-side storage configuration is the step teams script and rarely trust. The[Everpure Cloud VM Extension](https://blog.everpuredata.com/news-events/announcing-general-availability-of-everpure-cloud-vm-extension/) automates iSCSI configuration, MPIO configuration, target connectivity, and volume mounting. It deploys through Azure Resource Manager, Bicep, and Terraform, so host configuration belongs to the deployment pipeline rather than a hand-maintained script.


[Read the Everpure Cloud Azure Native announcement](https://blog.everpuredata.com/products/everpure-cloud-azure-native-expands/)


## **Fewer handoffs in Pure1**


### Upgrade the fleet without booking support time


Staying current has been a scheduling problem more than a technical one. An assisted upgrade means booking support time, sometimes weeks out. Auto SSUs move the whole sequence to the Pure1 Software Lifecycle page and run it unattended: six clicks start it, and roughly 90 minutes later the fleet is current. It’s the same non-disruptive procedure an assisted upgrade performs, backed by the same support team. Admins who want checkpoints can set mandatory pauses. FlashArray is covered, including ActiveCluster pairs in synchronous replication, as is[Everpure Cloud](https://www.everpuredata.com/products/cloud.html) .


### Pull security findings into your own tools


Security teams already have a place for storage security data. What they’ve lacked is a way to get it there without a person in the middle. Security Assessment Public APIs now expose appliance-level insights across FlashArray and[FlashBlade](https://www.everpuredata.com/products/unstructured-data-storage.html) ®, open security anomalies, and fleet-wide CVE exposure with severity scores and affected Purity versions. Output feeds a SIEM, a vulnerability management platform, or an automated incident response pipeline, with no custom integration code.


### Prepare a new array without the email thread


Installation prep has historically been fragmented across external forms, opaque orders, and scheduling threads in email. Pure1 now carries the installation lifecycle from the Orders page. Teams see a detailed bill of materials before the shipment arrives; capture device, network, and power readiness in place; and submit preferred install dates directly. Reschedule and cancel are first-class actions, and the page retains up to two years of procurement history.


[Try it out today](http://pure1.purestorage.com/) ! (Pure1 login required)


## **A more proactive service model**


Enterprise infrastructure has become more complex, and teams expect more than a traditional support model. Everpure Enterprise Advantage Services is a new tiered subscription that extends beyond support. It combines differentiated support, proactive operational guidance, advanced insights, executive reporting, and coordinated service management into one experience. Tiered service levels let teams choose the depth of engagement that fits: operational health reviews, capacity planning, upgrade readiness, risk assessments, best-practice recommendations, and executive business reviews. The value arrives across the ownership journey rather than only when something breaks.


## **The bigger picture**


Taken together, these releases point to the same thing: less manual effort between a team and the outcome it wants. Denser capacity, one control plane over a larger fleet, a shorter path off VMware, and consistent protection for Kubernetes data all pull in that direction.
